sentences.text: Second material aspect for consideration herein, that, as per the assertions of the petitioners of MVC No.1395/2019, there is a direct nexus between the accidental injuries and subsequent death of Fayaz Khan.

But to substantiate the same, no further medical documents or P.M. report or the evidence of the doctor are available on record, to prove the chain of circumstances, to show that there was a direct nexus between the accidental injuries and subsequent death of Fayaz Khan.
As per records on 9.9.2019 accident in question had taken place.
Subsequently, during the proceedings of the case on 22.12.2021 the said Fayaz Khan had died at his residence.
In such a situation, strong medical documentary evidence is available on record for 23 SCCH-18 MVC 6800/2019 & MVC 1395/2020 consideration.

But at the time of evidence of PW2 except wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills, prescriptions and x-rays as per Ex.P12 to Ex.P16, no other further medical documents placed on record to show that, due to the sole accidental injuries, the said Fayaz Khan had died.

On going through the nature of the injuries noted in the wound certificate, as well as in the discharge summary marked at Ex.P12 & Ex.P13, will not create confidence to believe the stand of the legal heirs of the deceased Fayaz Khan, with respect to the nexus between the accidental injuries and subsequent death.
Ex.P13 case summary and discharge record reveals that he had admitted to the hospital on 9.10.2019 and discharged on 16.10.2019.

Except this document, no other further medical documentary evidence to show, even after the discharge from the hospital on 16.10.2019, the said said Fayaz Khan had taken further treatment, till his death.

Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW2, in para N0.2 stated, contrary to the discharge summary that, her father was admitted in the hospital and took treatment as an inpatient for a period of 3 months and subsequently he had died.
Further, contrary to her earlier version, she stated that, her father had died in the residence itself.
Added to this, she answered that, she has not produced P.M. report as well as death summary.
Added to this, she admitted that, in the final report there is no whisper that, her father had died due to the accidental injuries.
On appereciation of all these material documents and evidence clearly speak that, there is no nexus betwen the accidental injuries and subsequent death of Fayaz Khan.

34. Consequently, the petitioner- Sabiha of MVC No.6800/2019 and deceased petitiner by name Fayaz Khan in MVC No.1395/2020 had sustained grievous injuries.
But to prove the nexus between the accidental injuries and death of Fayaz Khan, in connection wiht the additional issue No.1, no satisfactory evidence placed on record for appreciation.

Hence, without making much discussions on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in both the cases are in the Affirmative and additional issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.

Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner in MVC 6800/2019-Sabiha about the injuries sustained by her, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

37. In the light of the preposition laid down in the above case, it is also relevant to note that, 27 SCCH-18 MVC 6800/2019 & MVC 1395/2020 "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
